e-4406.knowledge_point: Multiplying Two Matrices When They Are Conformable
e-4406.worked_solution:
Here, $C$ is a $2 \times 3$ matrix and $D$ is a $3 \times 2$ matrix. 

There are $3$ columns in $C$ and $3$ rows in $D,$ so $C$ and $D$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \color{green}{\fbox{3}}}{C} \underset{\color{green}\checkmark}{\cdot} \underset{{\color{green}\fbox{3}} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{D} = 
	\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{CD}
$$

Let's compute $CD,$ one element at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,-4=1\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot 2+0\cdot (-3) \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,1=1\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 0+0\cdot 2 \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -1 & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,-1=2\cdot 0+1\cdot 2+1\cdot (-3) \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}], &  & \,4=2\cdot 1+1\cdot 0+1\cdot 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}]$

e-4407.knowledge_point: Finding an Entry of the Product of Two Matrices
e-4407.problem:
Let $C=AB.$ What is the value of $c_{32}$, if

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4407.worked_solution:
Multiplying the $3$rd row in $A$ by the $2$nd column in $B$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =1\cdot 4+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-4 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-5885.knowledge_point: Multiplying a Column-Vector By a Row-Vector
e-5885.worked_solution:
Here, the first factor is a $3 \times 1$ matrix and the second factor is a $1 \times 2$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in the first matrix and $1$ row in the second matrix, so the product is well defined:

$$
\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{3} \times {\color{green}\fbox{1}} {\color{green}\checkmark} {\color{green}\fbox{1}} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} = 
	\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{3} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}
$$

Computing the product, we have

$$
\eqalign {
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
       -1 \
 	0 \
        -2
    }
    \right\rbrack

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        2 & -5
    }
    \right\rbrack

	&= 

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        (-1)\cdot 2 & (-1)\cdot (-5) \
        0\cdot 2 & 0\cdot (-5)\
        (-2)\cdot 2 & (-2)\cdot (-5)
    }
    \right\rbrack \[5pt]

	&=

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
       -2 & 5 \
       0 &  0 \
       -4 &  10 
    }
    \right\rbrack 
}
$$

$$
{E}_{2\times \boxed{\text{4}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{F}_{\boxed{\text{4}}\times 2}={EF}_{2\times 2}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,2=1\cdot 4+(-2)\cdot (-3)+4\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 0 \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 18 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,18=1\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+5\cdot 2 \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 18 \\ 15 & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,15=3\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot (-3)+0\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 0 \\  & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 18 \\ 15 & 9\end{aligned}], &  & \,9=3\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 1+1\cdot 2\end{aligned}

$$

$$

decision.explanation: Multiply each entry of A by the row B. The resulting rows are (0,0), (-2,-4), and (-3,-6), matching option e.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Here, $A$ is $3\times 1$ matrix and $B$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in matrix $A$ and $1$ row in matrix $B$, so the product is well defined:

$$
{A}_{3\times \boxed{\text{1}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{B}_{\boxed{\text{1}}\times 2}={AB}_{3\times 2}
$$

Computing the product, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0\cdot 1 & 0\cdot 2 \\ (-2)\cdot 1 & (-2)\cdot 2 \\ (-3)\cdot 1 & (-3)\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & -4 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{A}_{2\times \boxed{\text{1}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{B}_{\boxed{\text{1}}\times 2}={AB}_{2\times 2}
$$

Let's compute $AB,$ one element at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,-3=-1\cdot 3 \\  & [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,1=(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -9 & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,-9=(-3)\cdot 3 \\  & [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -9 & 3\end{aligned}], &  & \,3=(-3)\cdot (-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$AB=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -9 & 3\end{aligned}].$
